hints.title: Look for shared beginnings
hints.body: Words that share a prefix share the first few characters. Which data structure lets you walk those characters once and reuse that walk for many queries?

hints.title: A tree of characters
hints.body: A trie stores one character on each edge. Every node represents the prefix spelled by the path from the root to that node.

hints.title: Store counts at the nodes
hints.body: Insert each word one character at a time. Add one to the counter at every node you visit. Then a query walks its characters and returns the counter at the final node, or zero if a character is missing.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body: Create a root node. For each word, set node = root and loop over its characters: create or follow the child, then increment that child's count. For each query, set node = root and loop over its characters: follow the child or record zero and stop. If the loop finishes, record node.count.
